gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI Elite 300's advertised '4,800 W' is Power Lifting, which BLUETTI's manual limits to resistive loads and does not count as a start allowance for compressors. A fixed-speed 5,000 BTU AC therefore has to start within the 2,400 W continuous rating, and a starting draw of 2 to 3 times about 450 W fits inside that.
standout_why: I compared homepowerfacts.com (cited), lightsonlab.com (cited), our own page and the other top results. homepowerfacts gives a 1,050 W starting figure from Champion. lightsonlab gives 1,000–1,500 W starting watts for 5,000 BTU, says inverter units have 'almost no startup surge' and mentions soft-start kits. Our page says every station 'handles (1,800 W continuous and 2,700 W surge at minimum)' and lists the Elite 300 as '3,014.4 Wh / 2,400 W'. None of them says that a maker's headline surge or 'lifting' number may be a voltage-reduction mode for heaters rather than compressor-start headroom. None gives locked-rotor amps or says how long a station can hold a surge.
decides: This confirms the pick and does not change it. The Elite 300 can start a conventional 5,000 BTU unit because its 2,400 W continuous rating is about 1.8 times the top of lightsonlab's 1,000–1,500 W starting range. The page should not cite '4,800 W' as compressor headroom, and Power Lifting should stay off for an AC load. LG's own description of its inverter compressor supports the page's 'only with an inverter AC' framing for the overnight energy math. An inverter AC changes runtime, not whether the compressor can start.
candidates: LG LW6023IVSM (6,000 BTU inverter window AC)

findings.label: What the '4,800 W' figure is
findings.value: Power Lifting: for 'pure resistive loads rated between 2,400W and 4,800W'; 'actual output power remains at 2,400W'; 'not a startup allowance for motors or compressors'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 300 Review: 3,014Wh, 2,400W and an 8ms UPS switchover in a 58-pound box (StorageReview)
findings.note: StorageReview attributes this to BLUETTI's manual. It also quotes BLUETTI's FAQ: motor and compressor devices 'can draw two to four times their rated power at startup and could overload the unit.' I could not open BLUETTI's manual PDF: it exceeded the fetch size limit.

findings.label: Maker's own wording of the output rating
findings.value: '2,400 W output (4,800 W lifting) for heavy loads like microwaves and heaters'
findings.note: The maker gives the 4,800 W figure as 'lifting' for resistive loads (microwaves, heaters). The page shows no surge or overload-duration spec, and its Tech Specs section was empty when I read it.

findings.label: Price, BLUETTI US store
findings.note: From the storecheck.py product lookup of the Shopify variant 'Elite 300'. compare_at is also $1,199, so there is no sale.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.value: 2.67 kWh delivered from full to empty; 3.49 kWh to charge from 0 to 100 %
findings.note: StorageReview measured both with a Kill-A-Watt. 2.67 kWh is 89 % of the rated 3,014 Wh. That beats the page's 'about 2.56 kWh' (85 %) estimate. At a 450 W flat-out draw it gives about 5.9 h, and at a 240 W average about 11.1 h (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Inverter vs fixed-speed mechanism (maker's words)
findings.value: The inverter 'adjusts the compressor motor speed to regulate temperature'; a non-inverter unit 'turns the compressor either on or off'
findings.source_title: LG 6,000 BTU DUAL Inverter Smart Window Air Conditioner LW6023IVSM
findings.note: 6,000 BTU, 'Cools Up To 250 sq. ft.' LG claims 'up to a 40%' CEER advantage over the DOE minimum of 11 CEER. The page shows no minimum-speed wattage.
